property_summary: After any call to Put(_unlockTime) by an account, the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime in the reference contract is guaranteed to be at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., not earlier than now); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it to a past time (< block.timestamp) and thus violate this invariant for some fuzzed _unlockTime.

For any Put(_unlockTime) call, the contract's recorded Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is >= the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant that blindly assigns _unlockTime can make unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

After any Put paid call, the reference ensures that Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never strictly less than the previous block.timestamp at the time of the call (i.e., stored unlockTime >= block.timestamp), whereas the mutant can set unlockTime to an arbitrary provided value < block.timestamp and thus violate this invariant for some fuzzed _unlockTime.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) invocation, the reference contract records Acc[caller].unlockTime equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (i.e., never decreases below the current block.timestamp), while the mutant may store the raw _unlockTime allowing Acc[caller].unlockTime to be strictly less than the block.timestamp; the test detects this by calling Put with a fuzzed _unlockTime and then asserting the stored unlockTime is >= block.timestamp after the call.

For any Put(_unlockTime) call, if the caller provides an _unlockTime that is in the future (>= current block.timestamp), the contract stores exactly that provided value; the mutant that ignores the block.timestamp comparison will still store that value (so rule holds) — instead, choose the complementary rule: whenever a caller supplies an _unlockTime that is in the past (< block.timestamp), the reference contract will store a value >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now), while the mutant may store the past value, violating this invariant.

After any caller successfully calls Put sending any non-negative ether and any _unlockTime, the caller's recorded unlockTime in the reference contract is at least the block.timestamp at which Put returned (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp), whereas the mutant sets unlockTime == block.timestamp unconditionally which can make it strictly less than expected when caller passed a future _unlockTime (breaking the rule).

For any caller and any deposit/payable amount and provided _unlockTime, after calling Put the recorded unlockTime in the reference is never less than the block timestamp at the time Put returns (it is max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)), whereas the mutant unconditionally sets it to block.timestamp and thus can make it strictly smaller when the caller requested a future unlock time.

For any caller, amount and requested _unlockTime, after calling Put the stored unlockTime for that caller is at least the provided _unlockTime (i.e. acc.unlockTime >= _unlockTime); the mutant that forces acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp can violate this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller, amount and requested _unlockTime, if the caller supplies an _unlockTime strictly in the future then after Put returns the stored unlockTime for that caller equals that supplied _unlockTime (the reference preserves a future requested unlockTime, the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp breaks this).

For any caller, after calling Put with any _unlockTime and sending any non-negative value, the reference contract guarantees that the stored unlockTime for that caller is at least the block.timestamp at return (i.e., not in the past relative to the return time) — the mutant that unconditionally sets acc.unlockTime = block.timestamp can make the recorded unlockTime equal to an earlier block.timestamp if Put was invoked in a future-timestamped block (the reference would have preserved a larger provided future _unlockTime), thus violating this when the fuzzer supplies a future _unlockTime.

For every call to Put by any sender with any msg.value, the reference contract never increases the sender's recorded balance by more than msg.value (i.e., Acc[sender].balance - prior_balance == msg.value and the call always succeeds); the mutant can corrupt this by reordering the increment and require leading to double-add or unexpected behavior when a callee reverts, so there exist inputs where the mutant's post-call balance differs.

For any caller and any msg.value, a successful Put call on the reference C never reverts and always increases the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance by exactly msg.value (i.e. post.balance == pre.balance + msg.value); the mutant that moves the increment before the require can make Put revert or misbehave for some inputs involving overflow/unchecked addition ordering, violating this rule.
